title: Geography Complete 4: Soils, Vegetation, Resources, Industries

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about black (regur) soils of India:
1. They are formed from the weathering of basaltic lava of the Deccan Trap.
2. They are rich in iron, lime, magnesium and alumina.
3. They are rich in nitrogen, phosphorus and organic matter.
4. They swell when wet and develop deep cracks when dry.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Black soils come from Deccan basalt and are rich in iron, lime, magnesia and alumina; the clay swells and cracks with moisture change. They are, however, poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 6; Majid Husain
questions.h: Regur = Rich in lime, iron, magnesia; Poor in N, P, humus

questions.q:
Statement-I: Laterite soils are generally poor in fertility and need heavy manuring for crops.
Statement-II: Intense leaching under alternating wet and dry seasons removes silica and bases, leaving iron and aluminium oxides.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Laterite forms under heavy seasonal rain; leaching strips away silica, lime and nutrients (hence the name from Latin 'later', brick) and leaves iron and aluminium oxides. This leaching is exactly why fertility is low, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 6

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the alluvial soils of the northern plains:
1. Bhangar is the older alluvium and contains kankar nodules.
2. Khadar is the newer alluvium that is renewed almost every year by floods.
3. Khadar is less fertile than Bhangar.
questions.e: Bhangar lies on higher terraces beyond the reach of floods and has calcareous kankar. Khadar is replenished by annual silt deposition and is therefore more fertile, so statement 3 reverses the truth.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 6

questions.q: The red colour of red soils in India is primarily due to:
o: high content of humus and organic matter
presence of lime and calcium carbonate
diffusion of iron oxides through crystalline and metamorphic rocks
questions.e: Red soils develop on crystalline igneous and metamorphic rocks, and iron oxide coating the particles gives the red colour. The soil appears yellow when it occurs in hydrated form.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 6

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Regur : Black cotton soil
2. Bhabar : Gravelly belt at the foot of the Shiwaliks
3. Khadar : Older alluvium of the Ganga plain
4. Kari : Peaty soil of Kerala
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Khadar is the newer, flood-renewed alluvium; the older alluvium is Bhangar. Regur, Bhabar (pebbly belt where streams sink) and Kari (peaty, marshy soil of Kuttanad region) are correctly matched.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 6; Majid Husain

questions.q: In a soil profile, the zone of illuviation, where leached material from above accumulates, is the:
questions.e: The A horizon is the zone of eluviation (washing out), and the B horizon receives the clay, iron and other materials leached from it. The C horizon is weathered parent material, and O is the surface organic layer.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (GC Leong); Majid Husain

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a soil conservation measure?
questions.e: Slash-and-burn (jhum) clears vegetation cover and exposes soil to erosion on slopes. Contour ploughing, strip cropping and shelterbelts reduce runoff and wind erosion.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 6; NCERT Class VIII Resources and Development

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about saline and alkaline soils (Usar, Reh, Kallar) in India:
1. They contain excess sodium, potassium and magnesium salts.
2. They develop in arid and semi-arid areas with poor drainage and strong evaporation.
3. They are mainly confined to the humid Western Ghats region.
questions.e: Strong evaporation draws dissolved salts up by capillary action, and poor drainage stops them leaching away, forming Usar or Reh soils in Punjab, Haryana, UP and Rajasthan. Heavy rainfall regions like the Western Ghats leach salts out, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 6

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Podzols develop under coniferous forests in cold, humid climates.
2. Chernozems are found in tropical rainforests.
3. Terra rossa forms on limestone in Mediterranean climates.
questions.e: Chernozem is the black, humus-rich soil of temperate grasslands (steppe and prairie), not tropical rainforests. Podzols (acidic, leached) and Terra rossa (red soil on limestone) are correctly placed.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (GC Leong)
questions.h: Cher-no-zem = black earth of the steppe

questions.q:
Statement-I: Gypsum is applied to reclaim sodic (alkaline) soils.
Statement-II: Calcium from gypsum displaces sodium from the soil exchange complex, which is then leached out.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Sodic soils have excess exchangeable sodium that disperses clay and seals the surface. Calcium from gypsum replaces sodium on the clay, and the sodium sulphate formed washes away with irrigation water.
questions.s: ICAR/Soil Health Card documents; Ramesh Singh Indian Economy (Agriculture)

questions.q: Which of the following crops are well suited to laterite soils of the Western Ghats and coastal Kerala, with proper manuring?
questions.e: Acidic, well-drained laterites support tree crops such as cashew, rubber, coffee and tea. Wheat, mustard, jute, sugarcane and cotton need fertile alluvial or black soils.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 6

questions.q:
Which of the following are considered passive factors of soil formation?
1. Parent material
2. Relief
3. Time
4. Organisms
5. Climate
questions.e: Climate and organisms are the active factors that act on the soil. Parent material, relief and time are passive, supplying the base on which active factors operate.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 6
questions.h: Active: Climate + Creatures; passive: Parent, Relief, Time

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Soil Health Card Scheme:
1. It was launched in 2015.
2. A card is issued to farmers every five years.
3. The card gives crop-wise recommendations of nutrients and fertilisers.
questions.e: The scheme began in February 2015 and cards carry crop-wise nutrient and fertiliser recommendations. Cards are issued on a two-year cycle, not five years, because soil nutrient status changes with cropping.
questions.s: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Soil Health Card portal

questions.q: Champion and Seth's classification of Indian forests recognises how many major forest type groups?
questions.e: Champion and Seth (revised survey, 1968) grouped Indian forests into 16 major type groups based on climate and vegetation, later subdivided into many sub-types. Simpler textbook schemes use five broad types.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India; FSI India State of Forest Report

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tropical evergreen forests of India:
1. They are found mainly in areas receiving more than 200 cm annual rainfall.
2. Trees shed their leaves simultaneously in one particular dry season.
3. Ebony, mahogany and rosewood are characteristic trees.
questions.e: Heavy, well-distributed rain keeps these forests green throughout the year. Individual trees shed leaves at different times, so there is no season when the whole forest is bare; that is a feature of deciduous forests.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about mangroves:
1. Sundari (Heritiera fomes) is the characteristic tree of the Sundarbans.
2. Pneumatophores or breathing roots help the plants obtain oxygen in waterlogged saline mud.
3. In India, mangroves occur only on the east coast.
4. Mangrove seeds do not germinate until they fall into the water.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Sundari gives the Sundarbans its name and pneumatophores solve the oxygen problem of waterlogged mud. Mangroves also occur on the west coast (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Kerala), and many species show vivipary, where seeds germinate on the parent tree before dropping.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 5
questions.h: Breathing roots stick up; seeds sprout on the mother

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched (tree : forest type)?
questions.e: Teak is a tree of tropical moist and dry deciduous forests. Thorn forests of the semi-arid northwest and Deccan hold babool, kikar and cacti, while deodar is typical of the Himalayan temperate zone.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 5

questions.q: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 is notable for which one of the following?
o: Creating Project Tiger as a statutory programme
Establishing the National Tiger Conservation Authority for the first time
Introducing Biosphere Reserves as a legal category
Reducing the number of Schedules from six to four and giving effect to CITES
questions.e: The 2022 Act merged the Schedules into four and added a Schedule for CITES-listed specimens, aligning domestic law with the convention. Project Tiger dates to 1973 and the NTCA was statutorily created by the 2006 amendment, so both predate it.
questions.s: PRS Legislative Research, Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Bill 2022

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their enactment or launch:
1. Project Elephant
2. Wildlife (Protection) Act
3. Project Tiger
4. Biological Diversity Act
questions.e: The Wildlife (Protection) Act (1972) came first, and Project Tiger followed in 1973 from Corbett. Project Elephant started in 1992, and the Biological Diversity Act followed in 2002.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; MoEFCC

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the zonation of a Biosphere Reserve:
1. The core zone is a legally protected ecosystem where activities are strictly limited.
2. The buffer zone allows research and education compatible with conservation.
3. The transition zone is the innermost zone around the core.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A biosphere reserve has core, buffer and transition zones moving outward. The transition zone is the outermost, where settlements and sustainable economic activity are allowed, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; MoEFCC

questions.q: Sholas are best described as:
o: Mangrove forests of the Godavari delta
Alpine meadows of the Western Himalaya
Thorn scrub of the Thar desert
Stunted tropical montane forests in the hollows of the Nilgiri, Anamalai and Palani hills
questions.e: Sholas are patches of stunted evergreen forest in sheltered valleys, interspersed with montane grassland in the high hills of the southern Western Ghats. They are quite different from the tidal, alpine or desert vegetation in the other options.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about protected areas under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972:
1. Grazing may be permitted in a wildlife sanctuary under regulation.
2. Grazing is prohibited in a national park.
3. A national park can be declared only by the Central Government.
questions.e: Sanctuaries allow some regulated human activity such as grazing with permission, whereas national parks do not. The State Government notifies both categories, so the Centre-only claim is wrong.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972

questions.q: Community Reserves in India are declared on:
o: any forest land by the Central Government without consent
only the land inside existing national parks
private or community land where the owners volunteer to conserve wildlife
questions.e: The 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act added Conservation Reserves (government land) and Community Reserves (private or community land). They recognise local custodianship rather than state acquisition.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 as amended 2002

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Mediterranean vegetation:
1. Plants are adapted to dry summers with small, leathery leaves and thick bark.
2. It is found on the eastern margins of continents.
3. Cork oak and olive are typical examples.
questions.e: Mediterranean climates have wet winters and hot dry summers on the western sides of continents between roughly 30 and 40 degrees latitude. Eastern margins have warm humid climates, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (GC Leong); NCERT Class XI Fundamentals Ch 14

questions.q:
Match the temperate grassland with its region:
Grassland: A. Pampas B. Prairies C. Veld D. Downs
Region: 1. South Africa 2. Argentina and Uruguay 3. North America 4. Australia
Which one of the following is the correct matching?
questions.e: Pampas are the South American grasslands of Argentina and Uruguay, prairies are in North America, veld is in South Africa and downs are in southeastern Australia. Remember that wheat and cattle belts overlap these grasslands.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (GC Leong)

questions.q: For a region to qualify as a biodiversity hotspot under Conservation International's criteria, it must have:
o: at least 500 endemic bird species and no human settlement
at least 10,000 plant species of any kind and no habitat loss
at least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species and have lost at least 70 percent of its original habitat
only tropical rainforest cover and over 3,000 mm rainfall
questions.e: The two tests are irreplaceability (1,500 or more endemic vascular plants) and threat (70 percent or more primary vegetation lost). India's hotspots are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar).
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; Conservation International

questions.q: Which one of the following iron ore centres is NOT correctly matched with its state?
questions.e: Noamundi lies in West Singhbhum, Jharkhand, in the Singhbhum-Odisha iron ore belt. Bailadila (Bastar), Kudremukh (Chikmagalur) and Mayurbhanj are matched correctly.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India (Minerals)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about coal in India:
1. Gondwana coal accounts for the overwhelming majority of India's coal reserves.
2. Tertiary coal of the north-east is of lower carbon content and has high sulphur.
3. Jharia coalfield, the main source of prime coking coal, lies in West Bengal.
questions.e: Gondwana coalfields of the Damodar, Mahanadi and Godavari valleys hold over 95 percent of reserves, while Tertiary coals of Assam and Meghalaya are young and sulphur-rich. Jharia is in Jharkhand; Raniganj is the West Bengal field.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 5; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about uranium and thorium in India:
1. Jaduguda in Jharkhand is a well-known uranium mining centre.
2. Tummalapalle in Andhra Pradesh has a large low-grade uranium deposit.
3. Rawatbhata in Rajasthan is a major uranium mine.
4. Monazite sands of the Kerala coast are a source of thorium.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Rawatbhata is a nuclear power station site, not a mine. Jaduguda, Tummalapalle (Kadapa basin) and the monazite beach sands of Kerala are correctly stated.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India (Minerals); DAE

questions.q: Which one of the following oil fields is correctly matched with its state?
questions.e: Naharkatiya near Dibrugarh is in Assam, like Digboi and Rudrasagar. Kalol and Ankleshwar are in Gujarat, so the other pairings are wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q: Which one of the following solar parks is NOT correctly matched with its state?
questions.e: Kamuthi lies in Ramanathapuram district of Tamil Nadu, so pairing it with Gujarat is the incorrect one. Bhadla (Jodhpur) and Pavagada (Tumakuru) are correctly matched.
questions.s: MNRE; Ramesh Singh Indian Economy (Energy)

questions.q: In land-use statistics of India, 'culturable waste land' refers to land that:
o: has been left fallow for one year or less
has remained uncultivated for more than five consecutive years but could be cultivated
is covered by buildings and roads
questions.e: Current fallow is land left uncultivated for one year or less, and other fallow for one to five years. Land untouched for more than five years falls in culturable waste.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 5 (Land Resources)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Resources are not static but dynamic in nature.
Statement-II: As Zimmermann argued, 'resources are not, they become', since technology and culture turn materials into resources.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A material becomes a resource only when people know how to use it and want it, so changing technology changes what counts as a resource. Hence resource status is dynamic and Zimmermann's idea explains it.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 5; Majid Husain

questions.q: The 'lithium triangle' of South America consists of salt flats in which of the following sets of countries?
questions.e: The triangle covers the Salar de Atacama (Chile), Salar de Uyuni (Bolivia) and Salar del Hombre Muerto (Argentina). Peru, Brazil, Colombia and Venezuela are not part of it.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography; MEA/Ministry of Mines lithium briefings

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Panchpatmali : Bauxite
2. Koderma : Mica
3. Khetri : Copper
4. Kolar : Iron ore
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Kolar in Karnataka is famed for gold, not iron ore. Panchpatmali (Koraput, Odisha), Koderma (Jharkhand) and Khetri (Rajasthan) are matched correctly.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India (Minerals)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Athabasca oil sands are in Alberta, Canada.
2. Ghawar, the largest conventional oil field, is in Saudi Arabia.
3. The Orinoco heavy oil belt lies in Colombia.
questions.e: The Orinoco Belt of heavy crude is in Venezuela, not Colombia. The Athabasca oil sands and Ghawar field are correctly placed.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (GC Leong)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about natural gas infrastructure in India:
1. The HVJ pipeline runs from Hazira in Gujarat to Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh via Vijaipur.
2. Dahej in Gujarat has an LNG import terminal.
3. The Kochi LNG terminal is located in Karnataka.
questions.e: HVJ links Hazira, Vijaipur (Madhya Pradesh) and Jagdishpur and carries gas to fertiliser and power plants. Kochi (Puthuvype) is in Kerala, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh Indian Economy (Energy); PPAC

questions.q: Which one of the following geothermal sites is correctly matched with its state or Union Territory?
questions.e: Puga valley is in Ladakh. Manikaran is in Himachal Pradesh, Bakreshwar in West Bengal and Tuwa in Gujarat.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh Indian Economy (Energy); MNRE

questions.q:
Statement-I: Sugar mills in India have increasingly shifted towards peninsular India.
Statement-II: Tropical sugarcane of the peninsula has higher sucrose content and a longer crushing season.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Tropical cane in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu has higher sucrose and a longer crushing season than sub-tropical cane. Cooperatives in the south add to this advantage.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 7

questions.q:
Statement-I: Weight-losing industries such as copper smelting tend to locate near raw material sources.
Statement-II: In Weber's least cost theory, a heavy loss of weight in processing makes transport of raw material costlier than transport of finished product.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Weber's raw material index is the weight of localised material divided by the weight of the finished product. A high index means locating at the raw material is cheapest, which is why smelting is placed at the mine.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Human Geography; NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 6

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cotton textile industry in India:
1. The first successful modern cotton mill was started in Bombay in 1854.
2. A mill was started at Fort Gloster near Calcutta in 1818.
3. The first mill in Ahmedabad was started in 1854.
questions.e: Bombay's 1854 mill was the first lasting success, whereas the Fort Gloster mill of 1818 did not survive. Ahmedabad's first mill began in 1861, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Spectrum A Brief History of Modern India (Economic Impact); Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of steel plants and the countries that helped set them up:
1. Rourkela : Soviet Union
2. Bhilai : West Germany
3. Durgapur : United Kingdom
4. Bokaro : Soviet Union
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Rourkela was built with West German help and Bhilai with Soviet help, so pairs 1 and 2 are swapped. Durgapur (UK) and Bokaro (USSR) are right.
questions.s: Spectrum; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 7

questions.q: Which one of the following aluminium smelters is NOT correctly matched with its state?
questions.e: Renukoot is in Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh, near Rihand's power supply. The others are correctly matched.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India (Industries)

questions.q: Which was the first large-scale fertiliser plant set up in India after independence?
questions.e: The Sindri plant in Jharkhand started production in 1951 as the first major fertiliser factory. The others came later or serve other products.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 7

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cement industry:
1. Limestone is the main raw material and the industry is raw-material oriented.
2. Gypsum is added to control the setting time.
3. It is a footloose industry that can be located anywhere.
questions.e: Cement is a weight-losing industry, so plants stay near limestone to avoid hauling bulky material. Footloose industries are those with light, high-value inputs, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 7

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about export processing and special economic zones:
1. Kandla was Asia's first export processing zone, set up in 1965.
2. The SEZ Act was enacted in 2005.
3. SEZs fall under the Ministry of Finance.
questions.e: Kandla in Gujarat led Asia in 1965, and the SEZ Act of 2005 came into force in 2006 with rules. SEZs are administered by the Department of Commerce, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh Indian Economy (Industry)

questions.q: Which one of the following industrial regions is NOT correctly matched with its country?
questions.e: Lorraine is the iron-ore region of France. The Ruhr, Donbas and Kuznetsk basins are correctly matched.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (GC Leong)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Tirupur : Knitwear
2. Firozabad : Glass bangles
3. Moradabad : Carpets
4. Sivakasi : Brassware
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Moradabad is known for brassware and Sivakasi for fireworks, matches and printing. Tirupur and Firozabad are correct.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India (Industries)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about oil refineries:
1. The Salaya-Mathura pipeline carries crude oil for the Mathura refinery.
2. The Digboi refinery in Assam is among the oldest in India.
3. The Numaligarh refinery is in Odisha.
questions.e: Digboi dates from the early 1900s and Mathura is an inland refinery fed by pipeline from the Gujarat coast. Numaligarh is in Assam, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 5; PPAC

questions.q: The tendency of an industry to remain at its original location even after the initial advantages have disappeared is called:
questions.e: Industrial inertia (geographical inertia) arises from sunk capital, skilled labour and infrastructure at the old site, e.g. the Lancashire and Sheffield industries. Agglomeration refers to clustering benefits, and footloose industries are not tied to raw materials.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Human Geography
